13356oi: Purpose answers the question “what for?”. If the person doing the main action is the same as the one achieving the goal, you use “para” + infinitive: “Ahorramos para comprar muebles” (we save, we buy).
d9wzzp: If the goal is achieved by someone else, you need “para que” + subjunctive: “Ahorramos para que nuestros hijos tengan un cuarto cada uno”. With the main verb in the present, future or imperative, the subjunctive goes in the present. The negation goes before the verb: “para no perder”, “para que no se pierdan”.

1i4fv4f: The subject is the same (“I” look, “I” pay): infinitive.

s1vjyg: Asking “¿para qué?”, moving “a” and speaking formally
uydxgb: The question “¿para qué…?” takes the indicative, also in indirect questions: “¿Para qué necesitan la garantía?”, “No entiendo para qué sirve este papel”. The answer can take “para que” + subjunctive.
kyrr3g: With verbs of movement (ir, venir, salir, bajar, subir, entrar), purpose usually goes with “a” + infinitive: “Vengo a firmar el contrato”, “Bajo a abrir la puerta”. In letters, notices and official documents you find “a fin de (que)”, “con el fin de (que)” and “con el objetivo de”, with the same rules as “para (que)”.

4c38d: If the person is already identified, for example by their name, the detail is only added, like a bracket, between commas.
